# 1 Maccabees Chapter 8 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_008_page_001.jpg

---

1. Judas heard about the Romans. Their reputation: immense power. Their policy: welcome all who come to them, make alliances and treaties with anyone who asks.
2. People told him about their wars — the campaigns they had fought in Galatia, how they had defeated the Galatians and put them under tribute.
3. What they did in Spain to take control of the silver and gold mines there.
4. How they had taken possession of the entire region through planning and persistence, even though it lay at the far edge of the world from them. Kings who had marched against them from the ends of the earth — they had crushed them, defeated them, and the rest were still paying tribute every year.
5. Philip and Perseus, king of the Macedonians, and everyone else who had raised arms against them — defeated, subjugated.
6. Antiochus the Great, king of Asia, had come at them with a hundred and twenty elephants, cavalry, chariots, and a massive army. Defeated.
7. They took him alive. They decreed that he and every king who came after him would pay a heavy tribute, give hostages, and hand over territory —
8. the regions of India, Media, Lydia, and the best of his lands — which they took from him and gave to King Eumenes.
9. The Greeks had once plotted to come and wipe them out.
10. The Romans got wind of it. They sent one general. He fought them, killed many, took their women and children captive, stripped their land, smashed their strongholds, and made them subjects — and there they have remained to this day.
11. Any other kingdom or island that ever rose against them — destroyed or enslaved.
12. But their friends, the allies who leaned on them — they kept those friendships faithfully. They became masters over kingdoms near and far. Everyone who heard their name feared them.
13. Whoever they want to be king becomes king. Whoever they want gone is gone. They rose to great heights.
14. And yet — not one of them put on a crown. Not one dressed himself in purple to make himself look grand.
15. They built a senate. Every day three hundred and twenty men sat in session, deliberating constantly on public affairs, governing the people well.
16. Each year they hand power to one man to govern the whole country. Everyone obeys that one man. There is no rivalry. There is no jealousy.
17. Judas selected Eupolemus son of John son of Accos and Jason son of Eleazar and sent them to Rome to make a treaty of friendship and alliance,
18. and to get Israel out from under the Greek yoke — because they could see that the Greek kingdom was grinding Israel into total slavery.
19. They traveled to Rome — an enormous journey. They entered the senate. They stood up and made their case:
20. "Judas Maccabeus, his brothers, and the Jewish people have sent us to establish an alliance and peace treaty with you, and to be enrolled among your allies and friends."
21. The senate received the proposal favorably.
22. This is a copy of the letter they inscribed on bronze tablets and sent to Jerusalem, so that it could stand there as a lasting record of peace and alliance:
23. "May all go well with the Romans and the Jewish people — at sea and on land, forever. May sword and enemy stay far from them.
24. If war breaks out against Rome first, or against any of her allies anywhere in her dominion,
25. the Jewish people will join them in battle with full commitment, as the situation requires.
26. They will not supply grain, weapons, silver, or ships to the enemy. Rome has decreed it. They will fulfill these terms without any payment in return.
27. In the same way: if war breaks out against the Jewish people first, the Romans will join them in battle with full commitment, as the situation requires.
28. The enemy will receive no grain, weapons, silver, or ships from Rome. Rome has decreed it. They will fulfill these terms in good faith.
29. On these terms Rome makes this covenant with the Jewish people.
30. If in the future either side decides to add to or remove anything from these terms, they may do so freely; whatever they add or remove will have full force.
31. As for the wrongs King Demetrius is committing against you, we have written to him: 'Why are you pressing your yoke down so hard on our friends and allies the Jews?
32. If they bring complaints against you again, we will take up their cause and fight you — by sea and by land.'"
